title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is scratch work in the genus-0 Teichmüller tower. It continues the previous page, which built line bundles L_i and L on M_{0,I} from 'cross-ratio' sections ξ_A with A ∈ P_3(I) and found torsion relations such as L^{⊗6} ≃ 1 for n=4 and n=5.

(1) Top of page: bookkeeping for the forgetful maps. For i_1 ≠ i_0 one has I \ {i_1} = {i_0} ⊔ (I \ {i_0,i_1}). The forgetful map p_{i_1}: T_{0,I} → T_{0,I\{i_1}} is the Teichmüller analogue of M_{0,K} → M_{0,I} for I ⊂ K.

(2) Two side remarks.
- 'O(4)^{⊗…} ≃ O(-2) ≃ Ω^1' on P^1 is presumably O(4)^{⊗(-1/2)} ≃ O(-2) ≃ Ω^1_{P^1}. This fits the square-root phenomena of the previous page (L_i^2 ≃ O).
- M_{0,I} ↪ ∏_i Σ_{J(i)}, with J(i) = I\{i}: the classical embedding of M_{0,n} into a product of lower moduli spaces or projective lines (cross-ratio coordinates).

(3) The real goal is the Picard group of the stack [M_{0,5}/S_5], i.e. of n unordered points on P^1 (M^! = 'rigidified' moduli). Grothendieck writes it as H^1(S_5, M_{0,5}; G_m), the equivariant Pic, and wants to compare it with H^2(T^+_{0,5}, Z). The latter is H^2 of the genus-0 mapping class group with 5 unordered punctures, which is what the exponential sequence on the K(π,1) stack predicts.
- Input 1: Pic(M_{0,5}) = H^1(M_{0,5}, G_m) = 0. M_{0,5} is open in P^1×P^1; equivalently it is the complement of a line arrangement in A^2 (the barely legible 'éclatement' remark presumably alludes to \bar M_{0,5} as a blow-up of P^1×P^1).
- Input 2: the fibration M_{0,5} → M_{0,4} = U_{0,3}. M_{0,5} sits inside U_{0,3}×U_{0,3} as the complement of the diagonal.
- Hochschild–Serre then gives Pic_{S_5}(M_{0,5}) ≅ H^1(S_5, O^*(M_{0,5})).

(4) The unit group of M_{0,K} sits in an exact sequence of S_K-modules
0 → G_m → H^0(M_{0,K}, G_m) → (Z^{P(K)})' → 0.
The right-hand term is a lattice of monomials in the (z_i − z_j) with zero degree in each variable. Its rank is n(n−3)/2 (5 for n=5, 2 for n=4, matching H^0(U_{0,3}, G_m)/k^* ≅ Z^2).

(5) Taking S_K-cohomology gives
H^1(S_K, k^*) = Hom(S_K, k^*) = {±1} (the sign character) → H^1(S_K, O^*) = Pic of the stack → H^1(S_K, lattice) → H^2(S_K, k^*) (Schur multiplier, Z/2 for n ≥ 4).
This is a standard method for computing Pic([M_{0,n}/S_n]).

The expected answer is Z/(n−1) for n odd and Z/2(n−1) for n even: Z/6 for n=4, Z/4 for n=5. This matches H_1 of the spherical mapping class group Γ_{0,[n]}. The previous page's 'L^{⊗6} ≃ 1' is therefore sharp for n=4 but not sharp for n=5.
errors: The lattice of unit classes is written (Z^{P_3(K)})'. The natural description is via pairs P_2(K): functions ∏(z_i − z_j)^{a_ij} with Σ_j a_ij = 0, of rank C(n,2) − n = n(n−3)/2. Either the transcription misreads 2 as 3, or the prime denotes a sublattice whose definition is not shown.

The diagram 'M^!_{0,5} – U_{0,3}×U_{0,3} over U_{0,3}' should be read as an inclusion: the complement of the diagonal in U_{0,3}×U_{0,3}. The fibre of M_{0,5} → M_{0,4} is P^1 minus 4 points, not U_{0,3}.
In the last line the index switches between S_5 and S_K; this is harmless, as K is the 5-element set.
Previous page: L^{⊗6} ≃ 1 for n=5 is true but not sharp. The torsion of Pic([M_{0,5}/S_5]) / H^2(Γ_{0,[5]}, Z) is Z/4, so L should have order dividing 4 there, unless L is a different class.

ideas.what: Picard group of the stack of n unordered points on P^1 computed as S_n-equivariant Pic of M_{0,n}, via Pic(M_{0,n}) = 0 and Hochschild–Serre on the unit group
ideas.modern_name: Pic of [M_{0,n}/S_n] (moduli of unordered points), equivariant Picard group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Arsie–Vistoli (2004) and related work on stacks of points on P^1; the equivalent H^2 of spherical braid / mapping class groups is classical (Magnus, Gillette–Van Buskirk)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only alludes to Teichmüller tower and Picard-type invariants of M_{g,n}; no such computation is published there

ideas.what: Unit group of M_{0,n} modulo constants as a lattice of monomials in z_i − z_j with an S_n action
ideas.modern_name: units of the complement of the braid arrangement / cross-ratio lattice
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (hyperplane arrangements; e.g. Brown's work on M_{0,n} units)

ideas.what: Comparison of algebraic Pic of the stack with H^2 of the Teichmüller groupoid T^+_{0,5}
ideas.modern_name: Pic(M) ≅ H^2(Γ, Z) for K(π,1) moduli stacks (exponential sequence)

deep.surprise_reason: These are fragmentary computations of the Picard group of the moduli stack of 5 unordered points on P^1 by standard group-cohomology methods. The results are known (H_1 of spherical mapping class groups, Arsie–Vistoli). The page shows Grothendieck's interest in Pic of the Teichmüller tower around 1978–84, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'M_{0,5} à corps d'éclatement : fonction en P1×P1' is more plausibly something like 'à coups d'éclatements : ouvert en P1×P1', referring to M_{0,5} as an open set of P^1×P^1 (blow-up picture of \bar M_{0,5}).
'(Z^{P_3(K)})'' may be P_2(K), given that the lattice rank must be n(n−3)/2.
'M_{0,[-K-]}^{\natural}' in the exact sequence is probably M_{0,K}^! (rigidified).
